question.text: Himalayan Debt AIF has 30% of its corpus contributed by a single NBFC (RBI-regulated). Under the SFA implementation standards (per SEBI Oct 2024 circular), specific due diligence is triggered to prevent evergreening. The threshold of RBI-regulated investor's corpus contribution that activates this DD is:

answer.text: More than 25% of corpus (either individually or together with a same group of investors)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI's Oct 8, 2024 specific-DD framework, RBI-regulated investors (e.g., banks, NBFCs) who individually or together with a same group of investors contribute more than 25% of the corpus of an AIF scheme trigger specific DD before investments. The trigger also applies where such RBI-regulated investors are associates of the Manager/Sponsor, or have majority/veto power in the investment committee. Look-through applies for AIF/GIFT investors. The Trap: Options A and B understate the threshold. Option C uses the 50% threshold that applies to the land-border DD scenario, not the RBI-evergreening trigger. Note: Workbook pages 367 and 369 support the specific-DD framework and the RBI-regulated investor 25% trigger; page 370 provides the contrasting 50% land-border threshold.
